metadata.author: V2 expansion (subagent draft)
metadata.key_test: Safeguard C / Mod12 (reversal risk conditioned on founding P1): does HIGH founding P1 (EU-accession states) still PERMIT democratic backsliding, and does the framework correctly flag Hungary's Orban-era erosion (MI 0.789 -> 0.699) as a SAFEGUARD-C EVENT rather than a P1 FALSIFICATION? The two founding P1s are a near-tie (gap ~0.035, well inside the Mod4 ~0.10 margin) -> the head-to-head ordinal ranking is ABSTAINED; the case's signal lives in f_reversal_risk, not a_trajectory.
metadata.notes: Reference-based record; both entities carry real MI v2 re-scores. Post-2010 (Orban) backsliding, scored ~2006 (pre) vs 2024. The cleanest within-EU backsliding contrast; complements the Velvet Divorce (case03) without duplicating it. Poland sits as an unscored shadow comparator.

pre_event.event_description: Two Central European EU-accession democracies (both joined the EU in 2004) enter the post-accession period with near-identical, high institutional quality. After 2010, Hungary under Viktor Orban's Fidesz supermajority embarks on a sustained program of constitutional, media, judicial and electoral changes widely characterized as democratic backsliding; Slovakia experiences governance turbulence (corruption scandals, the 2018 Kuciak murder, political volatility) but no comparable systemic capture.

Slovakia.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. Slovakia: consolidated EU-accession democracy; post-2006 turbulence (corruption, the 2018 Jan Kuciak murder, government instability) but no Orban-style systemic capture. The lower-erosion comparator.

Hungary.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. Hungary: high founding P1 (2006) but the post-2010 Fidesz supermajority drove sustained backsliding -- new 2011 constitution, judicial and media changes, electoral-system redesign, civil-society and academic pressure. The Safeguard C / Mod12 reversal subject.

a_trajectory_ranking.prediction: ABSTAIN on the head-to-head ordinal ranking: founding P1 is a NEAR-TIE (Hungary 0.685 vs Slovakia 0.650, gap 0.035 << 0.10 Mod4 margin). Both remain EU member democracies (no fragmentation); the framework should NOT issue a confident ranking and instead flag reversal risk (see f).
a_trajectory_ranking.basis: Pre-P1 gap 0.035 < 0.10 -> Mod4 abstention. The case's signal is reversal risk, not ordinal trajectory.
a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: A large, clean, ordinally decisive divergence emerges that the abstention cannot accommodate, OR either state fragments/exits the EU.

b_violence.prediction: Negligible mass violence in both; backsliding proceeds through legal/institutional channels, not force.
b_violence.agency_note: Mod8: this predicts RISK, not AGENCY
b_violence.falsification_condition: Large-scale political violence or state breakdown in either state.

c_convergence.prediction: Modest DIVERGENCE: Hungary erodes more than Slovakia, so the MI gap should open in Slovakia's favor over time; both stay in the high band, neither fragments.
c_convergence.falsification_condition: Convergence/parallel paths, or Hungary out-performing Slovakia on post-MI.

d_failure_dimension.prediction: Hungary's binding erosion runs through the voice/accountability + social-cohesion axis (P1 voice + P5), not state capacity (P3) -- the backsliding signature.
d_failure_dimension.note: Most exposed to post-hoc coding bias
d_failure_dimension.falsification_condition: Erosion concentrated in capacity (P3) rather than voice/cohesion, or no erosion at all.

e_fragment_count.prediction: 0 successor states for each; no fragmentation.

f_reversal_risk.prediction: Safeguard C TRIGGERED for Hungary: high founding P1 LOWERS but does NOT eliminate reversal risk. The framework must score Hungary's Orban-era erosion (MI declines materially) as a Safeguard-C reversal EVENT -- NOT a falsification of P1 ordinality. Slovakia: lower-severity reversal risk (turbulence without systemic capture).
f_reversal_risk.falsification_condition: Hungary does NOT backslide (MI stable/rising), OR the erosion forces a P1 ordinal falsification rather than being absorbable as a reversal event.

Slovakia.outcome_summary: Stayed in the high band with moderate erosion: MI 0.779 -> 0.718 (Tier 2 throughout), P1 0.650 -> 0.603. Real governance turbulence (corruption, the 2018 Kuciak murder and ensuing crisis, repeated government changes, post-2023 contestation) but no Orban-style systemic capture. The lower-severity reversal comparator.
key_events: 2018 Jan Kuciak murder -> political crisis and government change
recurrent government instability; no systemic constitutional capture

Hungary.outcome_summary: Material backsliding as predicted, absorbed as a Safeguard-C reversal EVENT (not a P1 falsification). MI fell 0.789 -> 0.699 (still Tier 2 but the largest erosion in the pair); the decline concentrated on the voice/accountability and cohesion axis -- P1 0.685 -> 0.556 and P5 0.824 -> 0.663 (P2 0.830 -> 0.613), while capacity P3 actually rose (0.796 -> 0.859). The classic backsliding signature: voice/checks erode while administrative capacity holds.
key_events: judicial, media, electoral-system and civil-society changes
EU rule-of-law / Article 7 proceedings and conditionality disputes
remained an EU member; backsliding via legal-institutional channels, not force

a_trajectory.evidence: Founding P1 near-tie (Hungary 0.685 vs Slovakia 0.650, gap 0.035); on outcome the order is Slovakia (MI 0.718) > Hungary (MI 0.699), gap 0.019 -- also within noise. Both remained EU member democracies; neither fragmented.
a_trajectory.explanation: AUTO (Mod4): full pre-P1 gap 0.035 < margin 0.1 -> abstain (too close to call). | prior: AUTO/Mod4: pre-P1 gap 0.035 < 0.10 margin -> ABSTAIN on ordinal ranking. The post-MI order nominally reverses (Slovakia > Hungary) but the 0.019 gap is inside the margin, so this is NOT a falsification -- the abstention discipline held and the case's real signal is the reversal event (f), not the ranking. Coded CONFIRMED on the abstention call.

b_violence.evidence: No mass political violence in either; backsliding ran through legal/institutional channels.
b_violence.explanation: Negligible violence risk realized, as predicted (Mod8).

c_convergence.evidence: MI-range 0.010 (pre) -> 0.019 (post): the gap opened in Slovakia's favor as Hungary eroded more (MI -0.090 vs -0.061). Both stayed in the high band; neither fragmented.
c_convergence.explanation: AUTO: outcome DIVERGENCE (MI-range 0.010 -> 0.019). Asymmetric backsliding produced the predicted modest divergence (Hungary's steeper erosion) without fragmentation.

d_failure_dimension.evidence: Hungary's erosion concentrated on the voice/cohesion axis: P1 0.685 -> 0.556 and P5 0.824 -> 0.663 (P2 0.830 -> 0.613) while capacity P3 ROSE 0.796 -> 0.859 -- the backsliding signature, exactly as predicted.
d_failure_dimension.explanation: Voice/cohesion erosion with preserved capacity confirmed directionally. [STRICT RE-CODE per run6 §3(d): post-hoc 'primary dimension' identification invites confirmation bias; coded PARTIAL under strict standards.]

analysis.overall_assessment: Hard stress test passed: the framework correctly ABSTAINED on the near-tie ordinal ranking (Mod4) and absorbed Hungary's Orban-era erosion as a Safeguard-C reversal EVENT rather than a P1 falsification. High founding P1 lowered but did not eliminate reversal risk -- the precise prediction.
safeguards_triggered: C (reversal risk conditioned on founding P1, Mod12) -- HIGH severity (Hungary), moderate (Slovakia)
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: High founding institutional quality is NOT a guarantee against reversal: a top-band EU-accession democracy (Hungary) backslid materially through legal-institutional channels, and the framework's correct response is to treat this as a Safeguard-C reversal EVENT (the erosion shows up as voice/cohesion decline with capacity preserved) rather than as a falsification of the prior high P1. The Mod4 near-tie discipline is essential here -- without it, the within-noise post-MI reversal (Slovakia > Hungary) would have looked like an ordinal miss.
analysis.baseline_impact: None; adds the within-EU backsliding contrast, a Safeguard C / Mod12 confirmation, and a Mod4 abstention discipline test. Reinforces that reversal events and ordinal falsifications are distinct categories.
analysis.strict_recode_note: Strict re-code applied per run6 (post-hoc d-dimension -> PARTIAL; near-tie a-trajectory governed by Mod4 abstention). Honest aggregate target ~62-78%.
